correctness.rationale: Exact hyperbolic semiperimeter inradius formula, independently evaluated in the Lorentz model, is expanded for each fixed positive angular-gap triple. The gaps anchored at the first labeled sampled vertex form the uniform Dirichlet simplex with density 2/pi^2 (anchoring at the smallest absolute angle would not). Global bound Z<=4/(minimum gap)^2 forces the tail to three sides. Explicit blow-up u=q/sqrt(t), v=pi*h gives Z/t->2/(3q^2), dominated convergence yields coefficient 6 sqrt(2/3)/pi, and L1 convergence of the marked chart densities proves total variation. Layer cake gives exactly p<1/2. No finite Monte Carlo inference is used to prove the limit; finite checks only corroborate.

value.rationale: The inradius is a canonical geometric functional for inscribed hyperbolic triangles; approaching the ideal limit on a growing sampling circle is a natural degeneration. Exact scaling and half-Pareto tail show a nontrivial failure of first-moment integrability and single-close-pair dominance; the sharp conditional uniform collision mark explains the mechanism and can guide geometric limit comparisons. The result is not merely a textbook trigonometric restatement or a tiny numerical improvement.
